title: NestJS Authentication Guards
outcome: Make NestJS independently verify Supabase access tokens and attach trusted identity before protected handlers run.
artifact: Authentication guard + verification service + current-user helper + protected /auth/me and task routes.
labSteps: Add Authorization: Bearer token handling in the API client without putting tokens in URLs/logs.
Extract and validate the bearer scheme in a guard with clear missing/malformed behavior.
Verify the token server-side using the supported Supabase/JWT verification path.
Normalize verified claims into an application user identity object.
Attach identity once and expose it through a typed decorator/helper rather than reparsing tokens in services.
Protect /auth/me and one task endpoint; test valid, missing, malformed, expired, and wrong-project tokens.
failureModes: Returning 403 when no valid authentication exists
mastery: Can explain why Next.js login is not enough for the API
Can prove identity is derived from verified token claims
principles: NestJS guards should verify identity before protected controllers execute.
Derive the authenticated user from a verified token, never from a user id supplied by the browser.
Attach validated identity to the request in one controlled place so downstream code can consume it consistently.
Return 401 for missing or invalid authentication and reserve 403 for authenticated callers lacking permission.
